name: General Tso's Tofu
steps: Press extra-firm tofu for 20 minutes, then cut into even bite-sized cubes and pat dry. Toss with the 55 g cornflour until each piece has a thin coating. Steam broccoli florets for 3–4 minutes until bright green and just tender; keep warm.

Whisk soy sauce, rice vinegar, brown sugar, ketchup and 120 ml of the measured water. In a separate cup, dissolve the 12 g sauce cornflour in the remaining 30 ml cold water. Keep both mixtures ready before frying.
Heat 40 ml oil in a wide non-stick pan. Fry tofu in one layer over medium-high heat for 3–4 minutes per side until crisp and golden; work in batches if needed. Transfer to a rack or plate.

Add remaining 15 ml oil to the pan. Fry garlic, ginger and dried red chilies for 30 seconds without burning. Pour in the soy-vinegar mixture, simmer 2 minutes, then stir in the cornflour slurry and cook another 1–2 minutes until glossy and thick enough to coat a spoon.

Add the crisp tofu and toss briefly so every cube is coated while some crispness remains. Divide among four plates with the steamed broccoli. Scatter spring onion and sesame seeds on top and serve immediately.
tips: Add tofu to the thickened sauce only at the end so it stays crisp. The reviewed photograph shows porous tofu cubes in deep red-brown glaze with dried chilies, scallions, sesame and broccoli.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
